lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Master. King. Our own Zeus down here. And you, daughter of Demeter — please, don't refuse a lover's petition.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: And what is it you want from us? Who are you, exactly?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I'm Protesilaus, son of Iphiclus, of Phylace — one of the Achaean expedition, the first man to die at Troy. I'm asking you to let me go back up. Just for a little while. Just to live again.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Protesilaus, every soul down here is in love with that particular idea. None of them gets it.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: But it isn't life I'm in love with, Lord of the Dead. It's my wife. I left her in our bedroom — we'd only just been married — and I sailed off, and then, poor wretch, I died the moment I jumped ashore. Hector killed me. And the longing for her is wearing me down, my lord — it really is. I just want her to see me. Even for a moment. Then I'll come back.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Protesilaus. Didn't you drink the water of Lethe?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Oh, I drank it, my lord. [pause] It wasn't enough.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Then wait. She'll come down here eventually, and you won't have to go anywhere.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I can't bear the wait, Pluto. You've been in love yourself — you know what it's like.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: And what good will one day of life do you, when you'll just be back here a moment later weeping over the same thing?

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: I think I can persuade her to come down with me. So instead of one ghost, you'll have two — very shortly.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: It isn't permitted. It has never been done.

lines.speaker: Protesilaus
lines.text: Let me remind you, Pluto. You handed Eurydice back to Orpheus for exactly this reason. And my own kinswoman Alcestis — you sent her up as a favour to Heracles.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: And you'd like to appear before that lovely bride of yours as — what you are now? A bare skull. No face. How is she even going to recognise you? She'll be terrified, I promise you. She'll run. And you'll have made the whole long journey for nothing.

lines.speaker: Persephone
lines.text: Well then, husband — fix that part too. Tell Hermes that the moment Protesilaus is up in the light, he's to touch him with his wand and turn him back into the handsome young man he was on his wedding day.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: [sighs] Since Persephone is in agreement — take him up and make him a bridegroom again. [to Protesilaus] But remember. One day. That's all.
